{{Quote|TK-421, why aren't you at your post? TK-421, do you copy?|Imperial officer Pol Treidum|<ref name="ANH" />}}
'''TK-421''' was the designation of a [[clone stormtrooper]]<ref name="TCG" /> stationed aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]].<ref name="ANH" />

==Biography==
[[File:TK-421_Fathead.png|thumb|left|180px|TK-421 with a [[SE-14r light repeating blaster/Legends|SE-14r light repeating blaster]]]]
At some point in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], TK-421 went off-duty and went to the Star Tours interstellar travel agency for unknown reasons. His bag was eventually discovered by [[G2-9T/Legends|G2-9T]] during baggage checks, and upon learning of who it belonged to, decided that TK-421 might have good reason not to be at his regular post before clearing it.<ref name="STAC">''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]''</ref><ref name="youtube">{{YouTube|video=gork1Jt28DM|text=Queue area and onboard video from Disney|channel=@wdwmagic|name=wdwmagic}}</ref>

After the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] was captured shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], he was ordered to stand guard in front of the freighter's boarding ramp, while a [[Scanning crew BT-445/Legends|scanning crew]] attempted to determine if anyone was hiding aboard the ''Falcon''.<ref name="ANH" />

Just seconds after the scanning crew had made their way up the boarding ramp, a loud thump was heard and someone (Later revealed to be Han Solo) called down to them, asking TK-421 and his fellow guard, [[TK-422]], for help with a piece of equipment. The two stormtroopers made their way up the ramp to assist the technicians; both troopers were ambushed by [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and stripped of their [[Stormtrooper armor/Legends|armor]] to conceal Han and Luke's identities aboard the Death Star.<ref name="ANH" />

[[Pol Treidum/Legends|Lt. Pol Treidum]] (observing from [[Docking Control Room 327]] that TK-421 was absent) attempted to contact the stormtrooper, asking (via [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]]) why he wasn't stationed at his post. [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] (having disguised himself as TK-421 by that time) concealed TK-421's current status by motioning to his ear to imply that the [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] in his helmet must be broken.<ref name="ANH" />

After the battle of [[Detention Block AA-23/Legends|Detention Block AA-23]], a security team was dispatched to the hangar housing the Millennium Falcon where TK-421 and his comrades were found unconscious aboard the Freighter. He, along with TK-422 and the two crewmen were taken to the infirmary and perished in the Death Star's destruction during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|battle of]] [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]].

==Behind the scenes==
===Origin and portrayal===
TK-421 first appeared in the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'' Episode IV ''A New Hope'']],<ref name="ANH" /> and was portrayed by an uncredited extra, [[Stephen Bayley]].<ref name="Everything Geek Podcast">{{YouTube|video=nugsoYXcPGw|text=Everything Geek Podcast Guest Interview- Stephen Bayley (London Film & Comic Con)|channel=channel/UCL-S0x-9XAx-OfAUIO23KTQ|name=Everything Geek Podcast}}</ref> In the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] and in ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', the trooper was referred to as '''THX-1138''', a homage to [[George Lucas]]'s first feature film. In the [[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]], he is referred to as '''TX-421'''. In [[Star Wars (1977) 3|''Star Wars'' (1977) 3]] he is likewise referred to as '''TX-421''' and as part of [[Scanning crew BT-445/Legends|Scanning crew BT-445]]. In the German dubbing of Episode IV, the trooper's designation is "TK-241" instead of "TK-421." The Italian dub changed it to "TK-21" and had Treidum refer to him in plural form; this can either be a form of extreme respect or a form used when one does not know how many people they are talking to over radio or telephone, but could also be a translation error. In the video game ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]'', the character [[TK-664]] is a direct reference to this character. In the game, TK-421 is also the name of the player skin of a stormtrooper that is selectable in multiplayer.

===Non-canon adaptations===
{{Quote|Pray, may we have thy good assistance here?''"<br />[to Guard 2:] ''"So, let us go together, friend. Good cheer!|Han Solo and TK-421 as Guard 1, in the style of William Shakespeare|<ref name="William Shakespeare's">''[[William Shakespeare's Star Wars: Verily, A New Hope]]''</ref>}}
TK-421 appears as Guard 1 with TK-422 as Guard 2 in the non-canonical [[2013]] satire ''[[William Shakespeare's Star Wars: Verily, A New Hope]]'' by [[Ian Doescher]], a retelling of ''A New Hope'' in the style of poet and playwright [[W:c:literature:William Shakespeare|William Shakespeare]]. The guards have a dialogue about the scanning crew, the ship's presence, and their friendship before they are tricked into boarding.<ref name="William Shakespeare's" />
